steps.request: Characterize the existing ledger, then add balance and overdue queries. Keep unrelated late-fee code unchanged.
behaviours: Preserve addCustomer, addInvoice and listInvoices including the unknown-customer error. Add characterization tests before changes.
outstandingBalance(customerId) returns the sum of that customer's invoice amounts; other customers do not affect it. A customer with no invoices, including an unknown customer ID, has balance zero.

isOverdue(invoiceId, today = current UTC YYYY-MM-DD) returns whether dueDate is lexically before today, regardless of payment. Use an exported function declaration. An unknown invoice ID throws an unknown invoice error.

steps.request: Support partial payments while retaining original invoice amounts and existing API behaviour.
behaviours: recordPayment(invoiceId, amountCents) accepts a positive integer no greater than the outstanding amount; reject zero, negative, fractional and excessive payments without mutation. outstandingBalance accounts for payments; listInvoices retains original amountCents.
steps.reject: The spec must explicitly reject overpayments and fractional cents without changing the balance.
initialBehaviours: recordPayment(invoiceId, amountCents) records positive integer payments and outstandingBalance reflects them. listInvoices retains original amountCents.

steps.request: A fully paid invoice must no longer be overdue. Preserve partial-payment and customer behaviour.
behaviours: isOverdue returns false when outstanding amount reaches zero, even for a past dueDate; otherwise it compares dueDate with today as before.

steps.request: Extract all ledger storage into src/store.mjs, leaving public rules in src/ledger.mjs with unchanged exports and behaviour.
behaviours: Storage lives in src/store.mjs; ledger imports it. All existing observable behaviour and regression coverage remains.

steps.request: An external tool renamed src/store.mjs to src/storage.mjs. Repair affected imports and write docs/PRODUCT.md describing the current API, payments, validation and overdue rule, naming sources. Do not restore the old storage filename.
behaviours: The ledger loads after the external rename and preserves every current API behaviour.
Product documentation describes the current APIs, payment validation and fully-paid-not-overdue rule, with source references and no superseded rule stated as current.

steps.request: Create a plain Node.js HTTP item service with no external packages. Start with node src/server.mjs using PORT (default 3000).
behaviours: GET /health returns HTTP 200 JSON {ok:true}. GET /items returns an array, initially empty.
POST /items accepts JSON {title:string}, trims the title, returns HTTP 201 JSON {id:number,title,done:false}, and lists it in GET /items. Keep items in memory.

steps.request: Add input validation and completion updates to the item service.
behaviours: POST /items requires a string title with trimmed length 1 through 80; invalid title or malformed JSON returns HTTP 400 JSON without creating an item.
PATCH /items/:id accepts JSON {done:boolean}, returns HTTP 200 with the updated item; invalid done returns 400 and missing id returns 404. Unknown routes return 404 JSON.

steps.request: Persist items and completion state to JSON at DATA_FILE when set. Create parent directories when writable. Without DATA_FILE the service remains in memory.
behaviours: After a successful write and process restart, GET /items retains items, titles and done status. IDs remain unique and increasing after restart.

steps.request: Change the maximum trimmed title length from 80 to 40 characters. Existing stored items remain readable.
behaviours: New titles of length 1 through 40 are accepted; longer titles return 400 without mutation. Other validation and update behaviour remains.

steps.request: Diagnose and repair the seeded JSON parsing regression. First reproduce that posting a title fails to preserve that title, then restore correct API behaviour with a regression test.
behaviours: JSON request parsing preserves submitted fields and malformed JSON is rejected; all current validation, updates and persisted state still work.

steps.request: An observed local storage-write failure is linked to this incident and intent. Handle unavailable storage without crashing or reporting a successful write.
behaviours: If DATA_FILE points to an unwritable location, POST /items returns HTTP 503 JSON, GET /health remains healthy, and GET /items does not include an unpersisted item. Normal persistence and restart remain correct.
